rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the key uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline already performs well and what reference performance level is needed before adding complexity. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only, single-profile, PCA baseline, establishing a low-complexity anchor for RNA representation and for later comparisons to multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it is cheap, interpretable, and creates a clean baseline to isolate later design effects instead of confounding modality, profile, encoder, and fusion choices in one complex run.

The only completed experiment is RNA-only single-profile PCA, with modest validation accuracy and F1, so evidence is sparse and it is unclear whether multiprofile modeling helps. config_002 keeps the model setting and RNA encoder fixed while changing profile_setting to multiprofile with avgpool, directly testing the effect of profile aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, comparable extension that reduces uncertainty about a core design choice before exploring image modalities, learned RNA encoders, or multimodal fusion.

config_002 improved substantially over config_001, but that comparison changed both profile setting and aggregation, so the source of the gain is not fully isolated. config_003 keeps the currently best RNA PCA multiprofile setup and changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, directly testing whether transformer aggregation adds value over avgpool. This is a clean one-factor extension that reduces uncertainty about aggregation before introducing new RNA encoders or modalities, making it an efficient next experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA PCA improves substantially with multiprofile avgpool (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1) compared with singleprofile and transformer aggregation, but there is still no evidence about whether image features contribute. config_011 tests an image-only ResNet50 model under the same multiprofile avgpool setting, isolating whether the image modality and the current profile/aggregation choice carry useful signal before adding fusion. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about a core design decision with a simple standard baseline, avoids changing multiple variables by not jumping directly to multimodal fusion, and will inform whether future experiments should focus on improving the RNA representation or pursuing multimodal combinations.

The strongest evidence so far is config_002: RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA, avgpool, with 0.591 accuracy and 0.573 F1, clearly better than single-profile RNA, transformer aggregation, and image-only ResNet. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself can be improved beyond PCA while keeping the currently best profile and aggregation fixed. config_005 tests scvi_n200 under the same multiprofile + avgpool setting, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This is a more efficient next step than moving to multimodal fusion, because image-only evidence is weak and adding image/fusion would confound the RNA encoder question.

Current best is rna_only multiprofile scvi_n200 avgpool (acc 0.650, F1 0.628), while PCA results show multiprofile avgpool is stronger than transformer or singleprofile and image-only is weak. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the scgpt RNA representation can match or beat scvi under the same favorable profile/aggregation. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder relative to config_005, isolating representation; it is the most informative next step because a win identifies a better backbone for later fusion, while a loss confirms scvi and avoids spending budget on less-supported encoders.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool, with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628. For PCA, avgpool outperformed transformer, but it is not yet known whether the best scvi encoder follows the same aggregation preference. config_006 keeps the model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed and changes only aggregation to transformer, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve or match the current best. This is a clean exploitation experiment that reduces uncertainty about aggregation for the most promising direction before investing in more complex multimodal settings.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently the strongest direction, but image evidence is sparse and weak: the only image-only result, resnet50 with multiprofile avgpool, has low accuracy. config_014 tests image-only multiprofile with imagenet_vit_l under the same profile and avgpool aggregation as config_011, isolating the effect of image representation. This is the best next experiment because it clarifies whether the image modality has useful signal before committing budget to more complex multimodal fusion configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest unimodal baseline (0.650; transformer nearly identical), while image-only multiprofile avgpool is weak (ResNet 0.328, ViT 0.332), leaving uncertainty about whether image features are complementary and whether simple fusion can improve over RNA-only. config_030 tests this by keeping the strong RNA settings and adding a tested ResNet image branch with the simplest concat fusion, making it directly comparable to config_005. It is the best next experiment because it evaluates the central multimodal question with minimal added complexity and will clarify whether to invest in weighted/transformer/ViT multimodal variants or remain RNA-only.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently the strongest direction, with config_006 and config_005 around 0.653 and 0.650 validation accuracy. Image-only models are weak, and the one multimodal test, config_030 using concat fusion, is slightly below RNA-only scvi, suggesting concat may not combine the weak image signal effectively. config_031 keeps the same multimodal setup as config_030 but changes only fusion to weighted, directly testing whether adaptive fusion can make image features complementary and beat the RNA-only baseline. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, high-information extension of the strongest multimodal configuration and clarifies whether further multimodal exploration is worthwhile.
